title: Interest in congressional engagement coexists with contact barriers and weak perceived responsiveness
source_unit: Ohio State University Institute for Democratic Engagement and Accountability Constituent Engagement Survey

denominator.unit: U.S. adults in a weighted online-panel survey; weights use 2023 ACS demographic and 2025 NPORS partisan benchmarks

congress_trust_most_of_time.unit: percent trusting Congress to do what is right most of the time

contacted_member_last_year.unit: percent reporting contact or attempted contact with a House or Senate member in the past year

representative_interested_in_respondent.unit: percent saying their congressional representatives are very or somewhat interested in what they have to say

would_like_to_talk_important_issues.unit: percent agreeing people like them would like to talk about important issues with Members of Congress

noncontact_member_does_not_care.unit: percent among respondents who had not contacted a member, citing that members do not care about concerns like theirs

noncontact_too_difficult.unit: percent among noncontact respondents citing difficulty

noncontact_member_will_not_change_mind.unit: percent among noncontact respondents citing expected nonresponsiveness

noncontact_too_time_consuming.unit: percent among noncontact respondents citing time cost

contacted_subgroup_email.unit: percent among the 219 respondents who contacted Congress, reporting email use

contacted_subgroup_in_person_town_hall.unit: percent among the contacted subgroup, reporting in-person town-hall attendance

ai_chatbot_effective_or_very_effective.unit: approximately percent rating an AI chatbot as effective for congressional communication

observations.method: Weighted descriptive survey designed by IDEA with the House Administration Subcommittee on Modernization and Innovation and House Digital Services; PureSpectrum administered an online panel survey, with full-sample margin of sampling error reported as plus or minus 3.1 percentage points. Contact modality estimates are restricted to 219 respondents who reported contact.
observations.uncertainty: This is a snapshot of self-reported opinions and behavior from an online panel; weighting does not remove nonresponse, coverage, recall, or social-desirability bias. The full-sample margin does not apply to subgroup estimates. Contacting is not verified, perceived interest is not an office response, and stated willingness is not follow-through.
observations.subgroup: Full weighted adult sample; noncontact barriers use n=782 and contact modalities use n=219. The report also discusses age, education, income, party, and channel differences, but the retained measures keep the denominators visible.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may report willingness while anticipating low payoff, and people who contact Congress may differ in education, time, political interest, resources, or social networks. Perceived congressional interest may reflect general optimism, party alignment, or prior contact rather than actual office behavior.

related_sources.claim: Congressional testimony summarizes the same survey's barriers, contact estimate, willingness, and two-way communication implications.

boundary: This record closes a descriptive contact-to-perceived-responsiveness layer for congressional engagement. It does not observe a constituent's actual office response, issue resolution, policy influence, satisfaction, remedy, later trust change, or durable political action, and it is not a verified contact log.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Ohio State IDEA technical report PDF downloaded and hashed; House testimony cross-checked for the core findings.
